# 🐧 Linux Systems & DevOps Administration Track

Welcome to the **Linux Systems & DevOps Administration Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth, hands-on systems curriculum covering Linux kernel internals, FHS filesystem architecture, advanced permissions (SUID/SGID/ACLs), process states, systemd services, networking diagnostics, and Bash automation.

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-kernel-architecture` | Kernel Architecture | Ring 0 vs Ring 3, system calls (`strace`), monolithic kernel, `/proc/version` |
| `01-filesystem-hierarchy-standard` | FHS & Inodes | FHS (`/bin`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`), inodes, hard vs soft links |
| `02-file-operations-and-navigation` | Navigation & Search | `find -type -mtime -exec`, `rsync -avz`, `tar -czvf`, `tree`, `stat` |
| `03-file-permissions-and-acls` | Permissions & ACLs | Octal modes, SUID (4000), SGID (2000), Sticky Bit (1000), POSIX ACLs (`setfacl`) |
| `04-io-redirection-and-pipes` | I/O Redirection & Streams | File descriptors (`0: stdin`, `1: stdout`, `2: stderr`), `2>&1`, `tee -a`, `xargs` |
| `05-text-processing-grep-sed-awk` | Text Processing (CLI) | `grep -rnE`, `sed -E 's/.../.../g'`, `awk 'NR>1 {sum+=$3}'`, `sort -k`, `uniq -c` |
| `06-process-management-and-signals` | Processes & Signals | Process table, states (R, S, D, Z zombie), signals (`SIGTERM 15`, `SIGKILL 9`), `kill` |
| `07-memory-and-cpu-monitoring` | Diagnostics & Load Avg | `/proc/meminfo`, `free -h`, `vmstat 1`, `iostat -xz`, Load Average (1m, 5m, 15m), OOM |
| `08-disk-management-and-filesystems` | Disks & Filesystems | `lsblk -f`, `df -hT`, `du -sh *`, ext4 vs XFS, `/etc/fstab` persistent mounts |
| `09-user-and-group-management` | Users & Sudoers | `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/group`, `useradd`, `usermod`, `visudo` |
| `10-package-management` | Package Managers | APT (Debian/Ubuntu), DNF/YUM (RHEL), repository sources, caching, GPG keys |
| `11-systemd-services-and-journals` | Systemd & Logging | Unit files (`.service`), `systemctl start/enable`, `journalctl -u service -f` |
| `12-cron-jobs-and-systemd-timers` | Scheduling & Timers | Crontab syntax (`* * * * *`), systemd `.timer` calendar vs monotonic events |
| `13-networking-and-troubleshooting` | Networking & DNS | `ip addr`, `ip route`, `ss -tulpn`, `curl -Iv`, `dig`/`nslookup`, `/etc/resolv.conf` |
| `14-ssh-keys-and-server-hardening` | SSH & Hardening | Ed25519 keys, `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (No root login, No passwords), `fail2ban` |
| `15-firewalls-iptables-and-ufw` | Firewalls & Packet Rules | `iptables` chains (INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD), `ufw` uncomplicated firewall, NAT |
| `16-shell-scripting-bash` | Production Bash Scripts | `set -euo pipefail`, trap cleanup handlers, command substitution, `getopts` |
| `17-security-selinux-and-apparmor` | SELinux & AppArmor | Mandatory Access Control (MAC), Enforcing vs Permissive, security contexts (`ls -Z`) |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 Linux SysAdmin gotchas (Load avg vs CPU, zombie cleanup, inode exhaustion) |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `example.sh` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.sh` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.sh` — Complete reference solution.

**Technical Internals & Architectural Notes:**

## 🎯 Key Directories
- `/etc`: Host-specific system-wide configuration files.
- `/var`: Variable data (logs in `/var/log`, databases in `/var/lib`).
- `/proc`: Virtual pseudo-filesystem exposing kernel state and process metrics.
- `/sys`: Virtual pseudo-filesystem exposing hardware device attributes.

## 🧠 Inodes & Hard vs Soft Links
- **Hard Link**: Second directory entry pointing to the same inode. Same inode number, survives original file deletion.
- **Soft (Symbolic) Link**: Small file containing the path string to target file. Has its own inode.

## ⏱️ When to use & When NOT to use

**Technical Internals & Architectural Notes:**
— Permissions, SUID/SGID & POSIX ACLs

## 🎯 Special Permission Bits
- **SUID (`4000`)**: Executes program with file owner privileges (e.g. `/usr/bin/passwd`).
- **SGID (`2000`)**: Files created inside directory inherit the directory's group.
- **Sticky Bit (`1000`)**: Only file owner or root can delete files (e.g. `/tmp`).

## 🧠 POSIX ACLs
`setfacl -m u:deployer:rwx /var/www` allows fine-grained access without altering primary user/group.

## 🎯 Process States
- `R` (Running / Runnable): Actively executing on CPU or in run queue.
- `S` (Interruptible Sleep): Waiting for event/I/O.
- `D` (Uninterruptible Sleep): Waiting for disk/hardware I/O (cannot be killed with SIGKILL!).
- `Z` (Zombie): Terminated process whose exit code has not yet been reaped by its parent (`wait()`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
retry() {
  local max_attempts=3
  local attempt=1
  until "$@"; do
    if [ "$attempt" -ge "$max_attempts" ]; then
      echo "Failed after $max_attempts attempts!" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    echo "Attempt $attempt failed. Retrying..."
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 1
  done
}

retry echo "✔ Retry helper execution succeeded!"
